about: Any CDA document modeled on a sample. A member has as many documents as the records give them -- one per day of service on each claim (encounter), as the claim's lines say, or one per member when the records are members -- every one the sample's document filled by the same config: the member's places from the member (the same in all of them, see 'levels'), the rest from that claim. Each document's id and set id are its own; everything else the sample has is copied, its clinical content included.
subject: claims

units.name: document
units.about: A document per day of service on a claim: care is written up the day it is given, so an office visit (one date) gets one, a five-day stay five, as the claim's lines say. A claim whose lines carry no date gets one; member records one per member.
units.missing: The sample has no ClinicalDocument to model documents on.

units.name: line
units.about: The procedures section (LOINC 47519-4) has an entry per claim line of the day: the line's procedure code and date, taken in turn from the sample's procedure entries; everything else in the entry (template, status, performer) is the sample's.

narrative.about: The section's table has a row per entry, written from it: the row the sample's entry points at ('reference'), its ids numbered for this entry and the entry pointing at them; 'cells' are said from the entry ({path} relative to the entry; a time as a person reads it), null keeps the sample's cell.

derive.about: Every document written is a new one: its id and its set id are its own.
Every procedure entry written is a new one: a new UUID for its id.

How the sample's procedure was done, where, and what it found describe that procedure, not the claim line's: the method and the body site are dropped, and an observation's result (which C-CDA requires) is unknown.
The sample's procedure in other code systems is not the claim line's: a generated code is written without its translations.
